test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7% per annum, respectively. Keshav borrowed an amount of ₹4,80,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Keshav after 2 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate difference per annum = 7% − 3.5% = 3.5%

Total difference for 2 years = 3.5% × 2 = 7%

Required difference in Interest = 7% of 4,80,000

Difference = (7 ÷ 100) × 4,80,000 = 7 × 4800 = 33,600

**∴ The correct answer is 33600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,80,000 for each bank

Rate of Bank A (RA) = 3.5% p.a.

Rate of Bank B (RB) = 7% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• Year 0 (P) Year 2 (T) ₹4,80,000 
 Bank B (7%) 
 Bank A (3.5%) 
• Interest Diff 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI paid to Bank A = (4,80,000 × 3.5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI paid to Bank A = 4800 × 7 = 33,600

⇒ SI paid to Bank B = (4,80,000 × 7 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI paid to Bank B = 4800 × 14 = 67,200

⇒ Positive Difference = 67,200 − 33,600 = 33,600

**∴ The correct answer is 33600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference in Simple Interest

When Principal (P) and Time (T) are constant, the difference in SI is given by ΔSI = (P × ΔR × T) ÷ 100, where ΔR is the difference in rates.

Total Amount in SI

The total amount (A) to be paid back is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Effective Annual Rate

The effective interest over T years at rate R% p.a. in simple interest is simply (R × T)% of the Principal.

1b
